name: City Council Adjourned Meeting of June 29, 2021
minutes_text:
APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  EL MONTE CITY COUNCIL ADJOURN REGULAR MEETING
  OF JUNE 29, 2021

MEETING JOINTLY AND REGULARLY WITH THE EL MONTE HOUSING AUTHORITY; EL
MONTE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY; EL MONTE WATER AUTHORITY; EL MONTE
PARKING AUTHORITY; SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE FORMER EL MONTE COMMUNITY
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY; HOUSING SUCCESSOR AGENCY; AND, FROM TIME TO
TIME, SUCH OTHER BODIES OF THE CITY WHOSE MEMBERSHIP IS COMPOSED
EXCLUSIVELY OF THE MEMBERSHIP OF THE CITY COUNCIL

1.  CALL TO ORDER: 6:01 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL FOR CITY COUNCIL AND AUTHORITY BODIES:

  Jessica Ancona, Mayor/Chair – present
  Victoria Martinez Muela, Mayor Pro Tem/Authority Member – present via zoom
  Martin R. Herrera, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Dr. Maria Morales, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Alma D. Puente, Councilmember/Authority Member – present

3.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA:

  m) Mayor Ancona
  s) Dr. Morales  5-0

4.  CLOSED SESSION:

  The City Council and the various Authority Bodies whose membership is composed
  exclusively of the membership of the City Council (collectively, the “Council”) will attempt
  to address and complete all Closed Session business between 6:00 p.m. and 7:00 p.m.
  If the Council completes all Closed Session business prior to 7:00 p.m., the Council will
  take a short recess and commence all Open Session proceedings promptly at 7:00 p.m.
  In the event the City Council is unable to address or complete all agendized Closed
  Session items by 7:00 p.m., the Council will hear all such remaining items toward the end
  of the meeting, immediately following Council Communications. Should any member of
  the public wish to address the Council on any agendized Closed Session matter, the
  Council shall allow such person to address the Council on such matter prior to going into
  Closed Session, provided that all persons wishing to address the Council on an agendized
  Closed Session matter shall fill out a speaker card and be subject to a speaker’s time limit
  of 3 minutes per speaker and further provided that the Council shall be under no obligation
  to respond to or deliberate upon any specific questions or comments posed by a speaker
  or take action on any issue raised by a speaker beyond such action as the City Council
  may be lawfully authorized to take on an agendized Closed Session matter pursuant to
  the Brown Act (Govt. Code Section 54950 et seq.).
   City Council Adjourn Meeting Minutes of June 29, 2021

Mayor Ancona invited members of the public to address the City Council on Closed
Session Items 4.1 through 4.10.

Mayor Ancona and the City Council recessed into Closed Session at approximately
6:02 p.m. Mayor Ancona and the City Council reconvened from Closed Session at
approximately 7:04 p.m.

Mayor Ancona and the City Council recessed into Closed Session at approximately
9:25 p.m. Mayor Ancona and the City Council reconvened from Closed Session at
approximately 10:36 p.m. All members of the City Council were present for Items
4.1, 4.2, 4.5, 4.6, 4.7 and 4.8 which were heard at the first part of the meeting. Mayor
Pro Tem Martinez Muela was not present during the second Closed Session
discussion for Items 4.3, 4.4, 4.9 and 4.10.

Assistant City Attorney Richard Padilla reported out of Closed Session with respect
to Items 4.1 through 4.10.

Just generally speaking as to all items updates were provided by various legal
counsels, City staff this is as to all 10 items, feedback given by the City Council but
as to each item but ultimately no final action taken on any of the 10 items.

  Channel Parcel (APN: 8578-020-001) located adjacent to and south of the I-10

  Betty Donavanik, Community and Economic Development Director; Jason

  Under Discussion:
  Both Price and Terms.

  54956.9(e)(1) – Conference with Legal Counsel – Anticipated Litigation – One (1)
  Matter.

4.3  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(1) –
  Conference with Legal Counsel – Existing Litigation: FEAH, LLC vs. City of El

  Bargaining Units Subject to Negotiations: El Monte General Unit (SEIU Local
  721); El Monte Police Mid-Managers Association; El Monte Police Officers
  Association; and El Monte General Mid-Management Unit (SEIU Local 721).

  City’s Designated Negotiator: Adrianna Guzman, Designated Labor Negotiator in
  consultation with John Nguyen, Human Resources/Risk Management Director;
  and Alma K. Martinez, City Manager.

  OPEN SESSION PROCEEDINGS

(Commencing at 7:00 p.m. or as soon thereafter as the City Council reconvene from Closed
Session/Short Recess).

   City Council Adjourn Meeting Minutes of June 29, 2021

5.  INVOCATION:  Chaplain Joseph Chen – I-Kuan Tao. Mayor Ancona

6.  FLAG SALUTE:  City Council. Mayor Ancona

7.  RECOGNITIONS, HONORS AND COMMUNITY INTEREST PRESENTATIONS:

  7.1  Recognition of Sergeant Jacob Salmon named Sergeant of the Year. Present

  7.2  Recognition of Officer Carlos Molina named Police Officer of the Year. Present

  7.3  Recognition of Julio Contreras named Civilian of the Year. Present

  Break at 7:15 p.m.
  Return at 7:25 p.m.

  Mayor Pro Tem Martinez Muela left the meeting at approximately 7:25 p.m.

8.  PUBLIC COMMENT REGARDING NON-AGENDIZED MATTERS:

  This time has been set aside for persons in the audience to make comments or inquiries
  on matters within the general subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the Housing
  Authority, the Financing Authority and/or the Water Authority (collectively, the “Council”)
  that are not listed on this agenda. Although no person is required to provide their name
  and address as a condition to attending a Council meeting, persons who wish to address
  the Council are asked to state their name and address. Each speaker will be limited to
  three (3) continuous minutes. Speakers may not lend any portion of their speaking time to
  other persons or borrow additional time from other persons.

  Except as otherwise provided under the Brown Act (Gov. Code Section 54950 et seq.),
  the Council may not deliberate or take action upon any matter not listed on this posted
  agenda but may order that any such matter be placed on the agenda for a subsequent
  meeting. The Council may also direct staff to investigate certain matters for consideration
  at a future meeting.

  All comments or queries presented by a speaker shall be addressed to the Council as a
  body and not to any specific member thereof. No questions shall be posed to any member
  of the Council except through the presiding official of the meeting, the Mayor and/or Chair.
  Members of the Council are under no obligation to respond to questions posed by
  speakers but may provide brief clarifying responses to any comment made or questions
  posed. The Council may not engage in any sort of prolonged discussion or deliberation
  with any speaker or group of speakers on matters that are not listed on this agenda.

  Enforcement of Decorum: The Chief of Police, or such member, or members of the Police
  Department as the Chief of Police may designate, shall serve as the Sergeant-at-Arms of

  4
   City Council Adjourn Meeting Minutes of June 29, 2021

any Council meeting. The Sergeant-at-Arms shall carry out all orders and instructions
given by the presiding official for the purpose of maintaining order and decorum at the
meeting. While members of the public are free to level criticism of City policies and the
action(s) or proposed action(s) of the Council or its members, members of the public may
not engage in behavior that is disruptive to the orderly conduct of the proceedings,
including, but not limited to, conduct that prevents other members of the public from being
heard when it is their opportunity to speak or which prevents members of the audience
from hearing or seeing the proceedings. Members of the public may not threaten any
person with physical harm or act in a manner that may reasonably be interpreted as an
imminent threat of physical harm. All persons attending the meeting must adhere to the
City’s policy barring harassment based upon a person’s race, religious creed, color,
national origin, ancestry, physical handicap, medical condition, marital status, gender,
sexual orientation or age.

Jane Myring – First off, I want to thank those who attended the lunch that we had that I
talked about a few weeks ago it was lovely. It was wonderful to be able to talk with others
because we have been so isolated it was a wonderful thing and last week I went to the
one Meals on Wheels you can tell people want to see each other they want to talk and
this is such a nice way to get with the community. The second thing I want to talk about
is fireworks I understand it is the safe and sane only if it used properly it is safe and sane
and we must remember that but I would like the public to be aware we have been having
fireworks for the past couple of months some of them are house shaking and we know
those don’t come from the safe and sane. I don’t have a good hearing thing for direction
from where they are coming from and that causes a problem I can’t call it in and say it is
coming from over there or there because my ears don’t work properly but for you have
good ears I think we should take the time and report those places where they are coming
from this has got to stop I mean it is so hard even on the 4th of July. I can tell you that even
at my stand at times we have to have someone sitting outside we had one that almost
land on top of the stand and we had to be aware of it. So, it is very important that if you
know that your neighbors are doing it it is kind of hard to say but don’t let them get away
with it they know better and I think that we should all take notice of it. Just take time to
report it and help us so that it doesn’t get so out of hand because it is out of hand now.

Eva Stoltz – Tonight I will start off with two thank yous to Councilwoman Martinez Muela
for letting us know at the last meeting that I attended that it was going to start late but she
had the decency to come out and tell us about it that is a first. Second thank you to
Councilman Herrera for supporting the women’s club lunch you impressed the women
there by introducing yourself. I understand the City lawyer can’t stop the Mayor on her rant
and raving on the former Mayor yet no one call tell her what a bully and pest she is by
using her chair to do this. Do we have a double standard here? Also, over $20,000 for two
movies how is this justified? Also, I would like to know what a traveling market is I think I
got a little explanation of it but wasn’t too good. The Mayor says we have to start tightening
our belts I think we should start up there with all of your perks starting with your car
allowance. How much did you spend on gas driving nowhere during the pandemic? Also,
phones that you have to have anyways. In the past I had a very good friend on the Council
she would laugh at the money being paid to her, her car allowance to drive from Lower
Azusa to Valley Boulevard it looks like being up there is your own personal ATM. Getting
back to the taco stands I have a picture of a resident on my phone selling beer packages
it was a tool box and you had your choice of beer or strawberries along with the tools in
there her name is there if anyone wants to see it. Is this selling liquor without a license?
Do any of you up there keep up with what is going on in our City? Like I’ve said our City

  5
   City Council Adjourn Meeting Minutes of June 29, 2021

is looking like a dump and you are allowing it to happen. The off ramp of the 10 freeway
on Garvey Avenue going west that has so much graffiti under there it has been there for
two weeks and not to mention the trash that is there. We had a wonderful pride celebration
at the farmer’s market and it was looking great but where is the pride in our City.

Steven Trumble – I'm Steven Trumbull and I'm the Library Manager for Norwood library
and sort of temporarily for the El Monte library and Tyler as well. The library has been
active throughout the year of the pandemic and it's still going strong. Almost all the libraries
are open to the public now. Tuesday through Saturday, some are open Monday through
Friday. Instead I want to talk about just a few of the programs that have, that are going on
now first of all lunch at the library, you can pick up a free lunch and breakfast at a number
of libraries including the El Monte library on Tyler Tuesday through Friday from 12 to 1pm
for kids and teens 18 and under reheatable breakfast and lunch first come first served and
the kids don't need to be there so if you want to come and pick up breakfast and lunch for
your kids who happen not to be with you, then, you're welcome to do that. The other thing
is the spring and summer Discovery Program from April 5th we started early through
August 8 you just sign up at the library or you can sign up online, you read books you
review books you're eligible for prizes and drawings and it's something that libraries all
across the country have done for years and years and even though in many ways, we
have been limited by the pandemic we have still kept this going on. In addition to some
outdoor programming has come with going on in some locations nowhere, very close by
unfortunately, we have a lot of virtual programs going on the July 2021 schedule has just
come out and we're going to have for tweens and teens, financial savvy, take a tour of LA
County's natural area parks, public speaking. There is a program called Work Ready for
adults that allows adults to sign up for a series of courses and among these are, find a job
if you're 50 Plus, workers’ rights with LA County Consumer and Business Affairs, living a
fulfilling career journey and so there are all kinds of things going on. And Tomorrow
speaking of the virtual programs and by the way this is all done on WebEx and many of
these programs need pre-registrations so login to LA Countylibrary.org and that's where
you can find the virtual programming that's coming in. Tomorrow an Evening with Luis J.
Rodriguez, who is the author of always running June 30 6pm on WebEx. You can sign up
by you can either you can sign up at la county.library.org/virtual hyphen programming, and
there should be a very interesting thing. Join us for a special evening he served as the
2014, Los Angeles Poet Laureate and is known for his work as a community and urban
peace activist mentor and youth and arts advocate for a general audience so library has
been closed for a long time but we've always been active. Thank you and do stop by
another we're open again.

Christian Garcia –I'm here tonight to speak in the view on our concerning matter of public
safety which affects us all in El Monte, as well as Los Angeles County. Now I hope we can
agree that crime has no boundaries, anything that happens from one of our bordering
cities affects us here in El Monte. George Gascon ran his campaign on bringing justice for
to Los Angeles and yeah, we need reform to see otherwise would be naive. However,
reform should not be a blanket policy, that doesn't consider facts or the history of person’s
case. Reform isn’t releasing dangerous criminals back into the communities and it's
definitely not going behind the back of the judicial system and victim families to making
plea deals for seven years for gang related murders. Now he says that he'll use diversion
programs, instead of incarceration. Apparently, the DA doesn't know that in order to be
eligible for divergence programs, you have to have charges filed. Now to be interesting to
know how many charges in El Monte have been rejected by the DA. How many of these
charges are the ones that directly affect us here in El Monte and quality of life, from the

  6
   City Council Adjourn Meeting Minutes of June 29, 2021

thieves of catalytic converters to vehicles taggers and home burglaries. Now some will say
that this is what he told the people that he was going to do during his campaign, which is
why he was elected. Now it is surprising to know that he didn't even make a special
directive known until the day he took office. He will also say well, George Gascon himself
states that he's using scientific data, and that his methodology will work. Well Gascon
should know that scientific studies are peer reviewed in order to back up the data, ensuring
legitimacy his studies are not, you actually paid for by the same groups that funded his
election, and who to this day advise him. On various occasions the DA has told the local
media outlets that those against him are part of this scary Republican net recall. While I
am not Republican my family members are all Democrats and the majority did vote for
Gascon and they already signed the recall petition. This past election both the mayor and
the chief of police of San Francisco, they endorsed Jackie lacy instead of him. Now can
you imagine if your own boss is not recommending you for a position that you applied for
and instead recommending another applicant. Now that speaks volumes. As of today, 22
cities have passed a vote of no confidence in Gascon and he not showed up to a city
council meeting to address the concerns of the council. Instead, his response via his
spokesperson is, and I quote “These are little red dots of red in a sea of blue. Ultimately,
it's pretty relevant.” Now prior to the crime doesn’t care if you are in a blue city or red city,
they don't care your sexual orientation, the color of your skin, your ethnicity, your accent,
your occupation and crime doesn't care if you are father or mother or brother or sister. We
can wait for any heinous crimes against another person, or worse, a child to occur in El
Monte. Now El Monte needs to be proactive. Therefore, I ask the City Council to make our
voices heard by not only introducing, but also by supporting a vote of no confidence in DA
Gascon at the next City Council. El Monte is made up of varying ethnic and socio-
economic backgrounds, we're not irrelevant.

Gabriel Ramirez – I know I wasn’t there at the last City Council meeting and by watching
I guess it is very different watching the meeting through online and here it is very different
because again because there is editing afterwards compared to the regular tv cable. So
last meeting was very when I saw the City Attorney I get it that there are members of the
public that want to speak however they were exercising their first amendment rights they
were not making any threats or whatsoever I understand that first amendment you have
the right to express your freedom of speech. And yes, I understand there is another one
that is pretty much says public comment regarding non-agendized item I understand that
there is that it was address to the public which it was and it is very despicable very
disgusting to have the City Attorney come in Rick Olivarez to silence two members of the
public and these are just trying to address to their Council again to everyone. So, I would
appreciate that he would issue the City Attorney an apology publicly. Second, as far as
for the meetings I have been noticing that when you are watching on cable and online I
know online you can see it for quite a bit but I guess but when you edit on Thursdays it’s
not what it is fully version of the meeting in public so I would really appreciate that it needs
to be fully corrected and not edit parts that are censoring or be the real form. And lastly, I
would appreciate that we have a new system because the mic systems even on the zoom
calls have been very poor this really needs to be addressed because again in Committees
for GG it is very lack to hear it on the microphone and our system isn’t adequately correct
sometimes there are some charges other cities that have a very good system on the mic
just want to make sure to address to that.

Cosme Jimenez – I just want to do a quick follow-up from last meeting which was stopped
by the City Attorney and it is not easy to be a City Attorney because you are going to be
a political attorney and City Attorney at the same time you have to please everybody at

  7
   City Council Adjourn Meeting Minutes of June 29, 2021

the same time the previous administration, the new administration so it is not easy being
a City Attorney. Also, he has to remember that City Attorney means City the whole City
we pay him to work over here he doesn’t get paid by the Mayor, the City Councilmembers
it is a citywide representation what is best for the citizens what is best for the Council he
has to be both sides at the same time. Also, just for reference and for record I want to give
this copy to the City Attorney so that Mr. Olivarez can read it was about a lady a high
school student from back east got in trouble because she named the for [inaudible] the
high school and she got in trouble she got kicked out of a group in the high school it went
all the way up to the Supreme Court and the Supreme Court sided with her 8-1 votes, 8-
1 not 1-8, 8-1 in favor of her that the item could be corrected and that she was right the
first amendment rights have to be respected.

Mary Ann Powers – Good evening Council staff. It was really kind of refreshing tonight to
see the recognition that you had. I've never seen or I've never heard the Police Officers
Association actually recognize their fellow officers and that was good to see and
congratulations to those officers, and thank you to all of our officers for what they do and
for putting their lives on the line to make us safe. Last week we spent a lot of time talking
about the budget and how to cut and how to save money and I really think that the
Councilmembers need to take a real hard look at all the disbursements before you approve
them so quickly. I was looking over some of the disbursements and one of them was one
vendor got $240,000 in the month of June, 25% of that $59,000 was the retainer. With a
retainer of almost $60,000 we still had another $180,000 in charges, what's covered by
the retainer? We need to start asking some questions so we need to start getting some
explanations, a retainer of $59,000 that is $708,000, a year, we could hire a couple of
attorneys for that. I'm sure they come to work for us for $350,000. I just, I find it a little bit
mind blowing that we so casually approve all of these expenditures. It's time we take a
look. and maybe we need to take a look and decide whether or not we need to hire
attorneys back and start our own legal department, because I'm sure Clarke Moseley, and
his staff, never made that kind of money. We need to take a hard look at how we spending
our money and I think that's another reason why we need to have a state audit, and we've
got attorneys on board on the Council now so that they would be even more helpful at
taking a look at how the money is being spent. And if we could do a better job, or legal
expenses are out of sight. Thank you. Have a good evening and a Happy Fourth of July.

Divided Association – Mayor, members of the City Council, and members of the El Monte
Police Officers Association, I am writing to you as a concerned EMPOA member with
concerns I have regarding our current El Monte Police Officers Association board of
directors. Most of our association members come to work day in and day out serving the
citizens of El Monte. The membership takes for granted the board they voted into office
will fully represent the entire membership, not only a few or themselves. Unfortunately, I
believe that is not the case. It is obviously clear, the EMPOA Board of Directors do not all
have the same mindset. You can ask any EMPOA board member and they will tell you
there is a separation amongst the board. With that being said, my concern is within four
board members and the decisions they make, not the board as an entirety. Below are a
few bullet points of some of the concerns I have. Board members are supporting and
endorsing Jessica Ancona and Vicki Martinez. Ancona and Martinez have NEVER voted
yes for anything relating to the EMPOA. As a matter of fact, both council members have
been extremely vocal regarding cutting police services, including the air support and
specialized units. Both have been very vocal regarding Police Department overtime and
recently sent the Sergeant of Arms for the council meeting home because Ancona did not
want to pay overtime, yet the position has always been filled for years, yet no concern for

  8
   City Council Adjourn Meeting Minutes of June 29, 2021

  the board. They have both been vocal at several council meetings regarding Police
  Department overtime. Overtime is never an issue with other city departments or the fire
  department budget. Although not an election year, the EMPOA board decided to give both
  Ancona and Martinez $5,000 each of your POA dues. Last year Ancona attended an anti-
  police rally with her daughter to the front of the El Monte Police Department during the
  George Floyd protests and riots. Ancona stood in solidarity with the protesters demanding
  the firing of El Monte Police Department officers involved in a use of force incident in the
  Klingerman apartments. Ancona and Martinez are both endorsed and funded by a prior
  chief of police. The is the same chief of police where an El Monte PD Air Support police
  unit has been seen parked in front of on several occasions. Although that board member
  was probably just paying for a “Dukes Brick” where his son plays. By the way, this brick,
  which supports one of the board members' son, was paid using EMPOA dues. So please
  send the board any financial requests to benefit your child. One of the board members I
  have concerns with has recently denounced the board's decisions they are currently
  making to administration in an attempt to successfully land a retirement job. Hopefully the
  memo for the TRAP assignment will fly soon. Today we honor Civilian and Sergeant of
  the year which is voted upon by the membership. Julio Contreras and Sergeant Jacob
  Salmon are examples of leaders of the El Monte Police Department. Unfortunately, Officer
  Carlos Molina was voted as officer of the year by 10 members of the EMPOA. What is
  disheartening is Officer Carlos Molina, formally detective Molina did not work one day in
  the year of 2020 due to being on administrative leave. Yet the El Monte Police Officers
  Association board made the decision to present this award in front of members of the city
  council. If you have any questions regarding my concerns, please ask any board member
  to answer the following concerns. You can also watch any council meetings on our city
  website which will clearly confirm Ancona and Martinez are no friends of the EMPOA.
